key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% versus bare SA516 boiler steel, delivering the best resistance among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings could help protect SA516 boiler steel from high-temperature oxidation through denser microstructures and protective oxide formation.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Laboratory testing linked improved oxidation resistance to reduced porosity, enhanced microhardness, and protective Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO oxides, while bare steel showed severe oxide cracking and spalling.
watch_item: Performance over 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles does not establish long-term durability under boiler combustion gases, erosion, or service stresses.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
